item.title: C printf Format Specifier Mismatches: Undefined Behavior & Practical Outcomes
item.description:
“C printf Format Specifier Mismatches: Undefined Behavior & Practical Outcomes”

The use of a format specifier that does not align with the type of the corresponding argument passed to printf results in undefined behavior. This means the C standard does not specify what should occur, and the actual outcome can vary significantly depending on the compiler, operating system, and even the specific execution environment.

It is crucial to acknowledge that printf is a variadic function, a characteristic that influences how arguments are handled. Specifically, arguments passed to variadic functions undergo default argument promotions. For instance, a char type is promoted to an int. This promotion means that certain mismatches might, in practice, yield seemingly predictable results due to this underlying conversion.
